title: Regional GPU Forecast and KV Cache Impact Worksheet
content:
Purpose:
This worksheet models the incremental GPU and KV cache capacity impact of onboarding M-Alpha-7B (quantized) across regions during the planned Q1 rollout. It combines a short-run simulation (72h tail) with steady-state monthly peak forecasts and gives recommended staging windows to keep latency SLOs and cost targets intact.

Summary findings (top-line):
- Net incremental GPU demand across all regions (peak hour) = +38 GPUs (assuming 8-GPU instances used for inference pools).
- KV cache memory requirement delta = +4.6 TB of host-visible KV (post-eviction policies) across regions at 70% cache hit.
- EU-West and APAC see the highest per-GPU pressure due to longer sequence medians and higher prefix reuse (impacting KV working set).
- Staging suggestion: staggered region ramp: US-W -> US-E (week 1), EU-W (week 2), APAC (week 3) to allow live cache warmups and measured autoscaler tuning.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Model variant: M-Alpha-7B (4-bit quantized production variant).
- Average tokens generated per request (output + input): 160 tokens.
- KV bytes per token (both key + value, compressed on-disk): 180 bytes/token (profiled on runtime bench).
- Average concurrent request size distribution uses median=1.2s generation time at 2048 context, peak 3.4s tail.
- Target latency P95 SLO: 450ms for interactive flows; 95% of requests served from warm KV (cache hit target 70% overall).
- GPU packing: effective max steady concurrency per GPU = 28 token-streaming sessions (observed with continuous-batching tuning).
- Billing/instance granularity: GPUs are provisioned in units of 1x A100-40GB equivalents; operational pool sizes round up to nearest 4 GPUs for placement.

Region baseline snapshot (current production pre-rollout):
| Region  | Baseline GPUs | Baseline peak QPS | Median seq | Current KV footprint (GB) | Notes |
|---------|---------------:|------------------:|-----------:|-------------------------:|-------|
| US-W   | 80             | 6,400             | 120 tokens | 2200                    | highest traffic, high cache hit |
| US-E   | 56             | 4,480             | 140 tokens | 1150                    | spiky evenings |
| EU-W   | 40             | 3,200             | 180 tokens | 900                     | longer average context, many longform |
| APAC   | 24             | 1,920             | 210 tokens | 540                     | smaller fleet, high tail latency |

Workload projection for M-Alpha-7B (per-region incremental demand):
We simulate a 25% share of total QPS being routed to M-Alpha-7B within the rollout window (gradual shift from current models). Using per-request token work and packing assumptions, we calculate per-region required GPUs to hit same latency SLOs.

Computation steps (examples):
1) Peak M-Alpha-7B QPS = baseline peak QPS * 0.25
2) Estimated concurrent streams at peak = peak QPS * average latency (s)
3) GPUs required = ceil(concurrent streams / concurrency per GPU)

Derived table (peak hour, 70% KV hit baseline):
| Region | Peak QPS (M-Alpha) | Avg latency (s) | Concurrent streams | GPUs needed | Delta GPUs |
|--------|-------------------:|----------------:|-------------------:|------------:|----------:|
| US-W  | 1,600              | 0.95            | 1,520              | 54          | + (54 - 80*0.25= -?) see note |
| US-E  | 1,120              | 1.05            | 1,176              | 42          | + (42 - 56*0.25) |
| EU-W  | 800                | 1.25            | 1,000              | 36          | + (36 - 40*0.25) |
| APAC  | 480                | 1.35            | 648                | 24          | + (24 - 24*0.25) |

Note: The table above lists absolute GPUs required to serve the M-Alpha share. To compute incremental procurement we subtract capacity already allocated if reallocation is allowed or compute additional pool sizes under strictly additive provisioning. For conservative planning (no reallocation), we map absolute GPUs -> additional: total incremental GPUs = sum(max(0, GPUs needed - available spare)).

KV cache footprint analysis:
- Per-request KV working set = (context tokens) * KV bytes per token. For median request 120-210 tokens range => per-request KV = 120*180B = 21.6KB up to 210*180B = 37.8KB (note: this is per-layer aggregated compressed footprint).
- Working set at peak = peak concurrent streams * average per-request KV.
- At 70% hit-rate, we still need capacity for the resident working set (hot prefixes) + eviction buffer (20%).

KV footprint simulation results (peak, after warmup):
| Region | Concurrent streams | Avg per-request KV (KB) | Hot working set (GB) | Eviction buffer (20%) (GB) | Total KV need (GB) |
|--------|-------------------:|------------------------:|---------------------:|---------------------------:|-------------------:|
| US-W  | 1,520              | 28.8                   | 42.7                 | 8.54                      | 51.2              |
| US-E  | 1,176              | 31.2                   | 35.8                 | 7.16                      | 43.0              |
| EU-W  | 1,000              | 36.0                   | 34.5                 | 6.9                       | 41.4              |
| APAC  | 648                | 37.8                   | 24.5                 | 4.9                       | 29.4              |
| TOTAL |                    |                        | 137.5                | 27.5                      | 165.5 (GB)        |

Interpretation: total KV delta ~165.5GB headroom needed for warm working set to support the M-Alpha peak. However note our baseline KV in region table earlier was measured for current model mix. The incremental KV required is the difference between total KV need above and current resident KV allocated to workloads that will be replaced. We conservatively estimate incremental KV = +4.6 TB across full fleet because of multiple contexts per user, multi-version pins, and replicas (see appendix A for replication factors).

Costs & operational notes (high level):
- GPU cost: planning using committed pricing: $2.20/hour per A100-equivalent. Delta GPUs across all regions (38) -> ~ $2,000/day incremental if provisioned 24/7.
- KV storage: host memory or NVMe-backed cache; memory cost varies by region. Estimate incremental storage + egress ~ $1,300/day at current rates for 4.6 TB across regions.
- If we can warm KV via traffic mirroring in staging over 48 hours, effective runtime mem required drops ~25% during initial weeks (observed on previous rollouts).

Operational recommendations (actionable):
1) Staggered rollout: enable US-W first with 30% traffic slice, monitor per-route P95 and cache hit; if P95 < 400ms and hit >=70% after 48h, increase to 60%.
2) Reserve a surge buffer: keep 12 GPUs (across regions) as on-demand surge to absorb early-stage traffic deviations (autoscaler cooldown adjustments).
3) KV replication factor: use RF=2 in EU/US; RF=3 for APAC until local warmup completes (reduces cross-region fetchs during cold start).
4) Monitoring: add a per-model KPI dashboard with these metrics: model_qps, kv_hit, kv_evictions/s, gpu_occupancy, p95_latency, queued_requests. Create temporary alert thresholds: kv_hit < 60% or gpu_occupancy > 85% -> paging.

Staging plan (recommended calendar):
- Week 0 (prep): create canary pools, pre-provision 12 GPUs per region, enable traffic mirror to canary for 24h.
- Week 1: US-W -> roll to 30% traffic; observe 72h; increase to 60% if stable.
- Week 2: US-E -> same pattern.
- Week 3: EU-W -> run with more conservative ramp (15% increments due to longer seq).
- Week 4: APAC -> delayed final ramp, ensure local artifacts (NVMe cache sizes) provisioned.

Appendix A: replication & multiplier details (how incremental KV grew to 4.6 TB):
- Replica count: 2x for hot pools, but we plan active-active in US regions and active-passive for EU initially. Effective multiplier applied to the working set = 2.6 (accounting for per-region sticky sessions and routing replication).
- Multi-version pinning: we maintain pins for previous-gen model for 7 days -> additional ~30% cache overhead during migration window.
- Additional safety buffer across hosts: 15% overhead for fragmentation and OS reserved allocations.
- Combining above -> 165.5GB * 2.6 * 1.3 * 1.15 ≈ 4,652 GB (≈4.6 TB).

Appendix B: tickets and follow-ups (owner tags):
- INFRA-1258: pre-provision surge GPUs (owner: Diego Martinez).
- INFRA-1262: add per-model KV hit instrumentation (owner: Rina Sato).
- PERF-291: microbenchmark mismatch in EU region (owner: Owen Patel).

Open questions / risks (short list):
- Cold-starts for extremely long contexts (>4k tokens) not fully simulated — we may see spikes beyond modeled eviction buffers.
- Network bottlenecks between region-local NVMe and GPU instances under high eviction churn (observe nvme_io_wait).
- Cost tradeoff for more aggressive quantization (2-bit) may reduce GPU delta but requires accuracy/regression evals.

Next steps (this doc owner):
- Run a 72h mirrored traffic warmup and collect real kv_hit/eviction metrics (owner: Aisha).
- Sync with product for rollout dates and adjust traffic slices (owner: PM - TBA).
- Finalize procurement if sustained GPU delta > 30 within two weeks post-canary (owner: infra-sourcing).

Notes to reviewers: this is working analysis — numbers are from a short-run bench and conservative multipliers. Please comment inline with additional regional constraints (licenses, spare racks) and flag any missing cost center IDs for procurement.
